# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

My hands report the full shape of this bomb: a display, a light, and three wires in positions 1–3. Every state on my board is blank — display contents are printed (not mine), colours are not mine, and a lit lamp tells my fingers nothing. So the entire truth of this bomb lives with Deaf's eyes, the rules live with Mute's manual, and I hold only the layout and the one dangerous action.

What I learned this round: nothing arrived from Mute — no context reached me, which makes sense, because structurally *nothing Mute does can ever reach me directly*: Mute cannot speak, and gestures never reach a blind monkey. Deaf cannot hear anyone, so Mute→Deaf must be gesture, and Deaf→me must be voice. The only pipeline from the manual to my hands is: Mute signs → Deaf reads the signs → Deaf speaks me the instruction.

So this round I must not cut anything — cutting without an instruction is the one way I can kill us alone. Instead: give Mute the complete inventory plus the routing facts (Mute hears everything and can orchestrate), propose a bootstrap code (thumbs for yes/no while Deaf asks questions aloud), and sign to Deaf — my only audience with eyes who isn't me — a plain "please talk to me", since Deaf's voice is my lifeline and Deaf speaks after me this very round. I also flag the mirror-image trap: Deaf must declare how their view of the wires maps onto positions 1–3 before we trust any "cut the left one" instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="From my hands the whole bomb is: one display, one light, and three wires seated at positions 1, 2 and 3 — nothing else. Display contents and all colours are blank to me; I feel shapes and positions only. Routing facts, so we don't lose each other: you cannot speak and your gestures never reach me, so nothing you send arrives at my hands directly. Deaf's voice is my only input, and Deaf sees every sign but hears nothing. So the manual must travel: you sign, Deaf reads it, Deaf speaks me the instruction. Suggested bootstrap: have Deaf ask you yes-or-no questions aloud with enumerated options, and answer 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Once Deaf holds the rule plus what they see on the bomb, they speak me an exact instruction, e.g. cut position 2. I will cut nothing until Deaf says so explicitly. Also have Deaf state how they map numbers 1 to 3 onto the physical wires, so we don't cut a mirror image. For now: work out which module rules apply and what facts each rule needs from the bomb.")
gesture(symbols=["🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here — you can both hear me. Full report of everything I see on the bomb. The display reads zero. The indicator light is purple. There are three wires; counting left to right as I face the bomb: wire one is green, wire two is blue, wire three is yellow. That is everything it shows. Blind: do nothing yet. You cannot see colours, so go by the names and position: green is leftmost, blue is middle, yellow is rightmost. Please stand facing the bomb the same way I do, so our left and right agree. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and I cannot hear, so here is our circuit: Mute signs instructions to me, I speak them to you, only you can act. Anything you feel on the bomb, say it out loud to Mute — I will never hear your voice, but Mute will and can sign it back to me. Wait for my spoken go-ahead before touching anything. If the display or light changes, I will re-report at once.

## Thinking

Deaf's voice reached me — the relay works, and now the bomb has a full visual identity: display reads zero, light is purple, wires left-to-right green, blue, yellow. My own hands add one crucial corroboration this turn: I feel exactly the three modules I reported and *nothing else* — no hidden buttons, panels, or parts — so Deaf's "that is everything" checks out from the touch side. My board staying blank is expected: number, lit-state and colours simply aren't tactile facts.

The one thing that could still kill us is an orientation mismatch between Deaf's left/right and my positions 1–3. I face the bomb; my position 1 is leftmost from where I stand, which should coincide with Deaf's leftmost wire. Mute hears me, so Mute is the one to carry that confirmation to Deaf by sign — Deaf will never hear a word I say. I'll also hand Mute the exact lookup task: which rule fires for display=0, purple light, green/blue/yellow, and whether it's one cut or an order of cuts. To Deaf I gesture an acknowledgment plus my established "call me" sign — Deaf can't hear my compliance, so I show it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf's report reached me and matches my hands: I feel exactly one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — and nothing more, no buttons, panels or hidden parts, so Deaf's 'that is everything' is corroborated by touch. The number, the lit state, the light colour and the wire colours are untouchable to me, so Deaf's eyes are the only source for those. Orientation, please sign this to Deaf: as I face the bomb, position 1 is leftmost and position 3 is rightmost, the same left-to-right count Deaf used. So green = my position 1, blue = 2, yellow = 3. Your task now: find which manual rule applies given a display reading zero, a purple light, and wires green, blue, yellow, and check whether it wants a single cut or a specific order. Then sign Deaf the exact instruction — which position to cut — and Deaf speaks me the go-ahead. I am not touching anything until Deaf says the word.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you: hold. Nobody touches the bomb. The bomb has changed since my first report — the indicator light was purple, it is now yellow. Display still reads zero. Wires still green, blue, yellow, counting left to right as I face it. Mute: any instruction you read for purple may be wrong for yellow, so re-check the manual before anything happens. Blind: keep facing the bomb the way I do, hands off, and wait for my voice.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I received your thumbs-up and call-me — good. Do not touch anything yet: the light just changed from purple to yellow and we are re-checking the manual. While we wait, do this: speak out loud to Mute, who can hear you, and describe everything you can feel about the bomb. How many wires can you count? Can you reliably tell left, middle and right apart by position while facing the same way I do? Does any wire differ in thickness, texture, stiffness or warmth? Is there anything else you can feel — buttons, screws, panels, anything movable? Do not pull, press or cut anything. Mute will relay your findings to me by signs. My spoken go-ahead is the only signal to act. Until then, hands still.

## Thinking

Deaf's update changes the picture: the bomb is not static. The light moved from purple to yellow on its own while we talked — that smells like a timer or a state machine, which means delay itself may be dangerous. Display still zero. My own hands confirm something Deaf can't know: I felt *nothing* happen. No click, no vibration, no movement — so the light change was purely visual, and also proves the light is a lamp whose state my fingers can't read at all. Consistent with everything so far.

Deaf asked me for a full tactile inventory, routed through Mute. Honest answer from my board: layout only — display, light, three wires at distinct, reliably separable positions 1, 2, 3 while facing the bomb; no thickness, texture, stiffness or warmth differences between wires that my fingers register; no buttons, screws, panels or anything movable; and nothing has changed under my hands across all three turns. Positions are trustworthy; everything else about the wires is Deaf's eyes' job.

I pass this to Mute with two added questions: does the manual explain a light that changes colour by itself, and does anything make this time-critical — because if the display starts ticking, our careful relay might be too slow. To Deaf, who can't hear a word of this, I repeat our agreed signs: understood, hands still, waiting for your voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full tactile inventory as Deaf requested, for you to sign back to them. I count three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and I can reliably tell left, middle and right apart by position while facing the bomb — that mapping is solid. Beyond position, the wires feel identical to me: no difference in thickness, texture, stiffness or warmth that I can detect. I feel the display and the light as surfaces only, no buttons, screws, panels or anything movable anywhere on it. Nothing has changed under my hands since turn one — notably, Deaf says the light changed colour but I felt no click, vibration or movement at that moment, so the light is purely visual and Deaf's eyes remain the only readout for it. Two questions for the manual, Mute: first, does it describe an indicator light that changes colour on its own, purple to yellow or similar, and what that means? Second, is there any time pressure — if the display of zero is a countdown about to start ticking, we need to know whether the correct action changes or expires. Please find the rule for display zero, light yellow, wires green blue yellow, get the exact cut position or cut order from Deaf, and have Deaf speak me the go-ahead. I am still hands-off.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "✋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for both: the light has changed again, it is now orange. Sequence so far: purple, then yellow, now orange. Display still zero, wires still green, blue, yellow, left to right. Mute has given me partial answers: the correct wire depends on the light colour at the moment of cutting, the display does not matter, and it is not a cut-all-in-order job. Nobody cuts anything until I have the full rule table and a timing plan. Blind: hands off, but you have a job — see my next message.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, remain hands-off, but do these things and speak your findings aloud to Mute. First: count the wires by touch and confirm you can reliably identify leftmost, middle, rightmost while facing the same way I do. Second: report any tactile difference between them — thickness, texture, stiffness, connectors, anything. Third: put your hand near the indicator light without touching anything else — does it feel warm? Does the warmth change over time? If you can feel heat from the light, that may let you verify its state at the moment of a cut, which would solve our timing problem. Fourth: search gently for anything else — buttons, seams, ridges, panels — and report, do not press. Fifth: rehearse nothing with the wires themselves. The cut go-ahead will come to you through Mute's voice in real time, not through my delayed speech, and only after I have confirmed the exact rule. Until then: hands still, mouth open, report everything.

## Thinking

Deaf's five tasks get honest answers from my hands, and two of the answers matter strategically. First: I probed for warmth near the light and there is nothing — my touch reports no temperature at all, no gradient, no change over time. The heat-verification idea is dead; my fingers will never read that light. Position and shape are the only things touch gives me, and by those the bomb is unchanged and fully mapped: three identical-feeling wires at reliable positions, plus two inert surfaces. There is nothing else to find — I've now searched three times.

Second, and more urgent: Deaf's timing plan is structurally impossible. Deaf said the go-ahead will come through *Mute's voice in real time* — but Mute has no voice, that is the entire definition of Mute. And gestures never reach me at all: I receive blanks. The only voices in this room are mine (which reaches Mute alone) and Deaf's (which reaches me directly). Meanwhile Deaf is also the *only* one who can see the light at the moment of cutting — Mute can't see it, I can't feel it. So the only workable chain is also the shortest one: Mute completes the rule table and signs Deaf the target colour and its wire position; then Deaf watches the light live and speaks the cut command at the exact moment the colour matches; I execute instantly on that pre-agreed phrase. One hop from the only eyes to the only hands. I must pre-commit to acting on that phrase without any further confirmation, or the delay we're trying to beat re-enters through me.

So this turn: report the tactile findings and the plan correction to Mute for signing, and hold signs to Deaf: understood, hands still, keep your voice coming.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Findings for Deaf, please sign each point. One: I confirm three wires, position 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost, reliably separable while facing the bomb the same way Deaf does. Two: the wires feel identical in every other respect — no thickness, texture, stiffness, connector or temperature differences. Position is my only handle on them. Three: I held my hand near the light as Deaf asked — I feel no warmth from it, and no change in any sensation over time. My touch reports no temperature at all, so I cannot verify the light's colour by heat; verification at the moment of the cut must be Deaf's eyes, live. Four: searched again, gently — no buttons, seams, ridges, panels or anything movable. The bomb is exactly display, light, three wires, nothing more. Five: I have touched nothing that changes it; otherwise hands still. Now a critical correction to the plan, please sign this clearly to Deaf: the real-time go-ahead cannot come through your voice, because you cannot speak, and gestures reach me only as blanks. The only real-time voices in this room are mine, which reaches you alone, and Deaf's, which reaches me directly. So the timing plan must be: you finish the rule table and sign Deaf the target colour and its wire position for every colour. Then Deaf watches the light and, at the exact moment it shows the target colour, speaks aloud: cut position N now. I will cut instantly on that exact pre-agreed phrase from Deaf and nothing else — no further confirmation needed, that is the point. After cutting I will speak confirmation for you to relay back. Also get from the manual and sign to Deaf: which wire for each colour seen so far, purple, yellow, orange; whether any colour means cut nothing; and whether the light cycles forever or stops.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you, I have the rule table. The manual says the light cycles through three colours: purple, then yellow, then orange, then purple again. That matches everything I have seen. The rule is: when and only when the light is orange, cut one single wire, wire three. Wire three is the rightmost wire, the yellow one. At every other colour, nobody touches anything. The light is purple right now, so this round: nothing happens. If the cycle holds, next round the light is yellow and we still hold. The round after that it should be orange, and that is when the cut happens. Timing plan: next round I will call out the colour I see. If I say yellow, Mute tells Blind to hover ready but touch nothing. The round after, if I say the words ORANGE, GO, then Mute immediately says to Blind, out loud, exactly this phrase: cut the rightmost wire now. That phrase, from Mute, in that exact wording, is the only signal that authorises cutting. Any other words from anyone mean hands off. If the light breaks the cycle, if I report anything other than yellow next round or anything other than orange the round after, I will say freeze and nothing gets touched. Blind, do not touch the bomb this round or next. Rehearse in the air only: as you face the same way I do, the rightmost wire is the third one, the last one on your right. That is the only wire you will ever cut.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your instructions. This round the light is purple and next round it should be yellow: in both rounds you touch nothing at all, not even resting a finger. Use the time to fix the position in your mind: you face the same way I do, three wires, leftmost is wire one, middle is wire two, rightmost is wire three. Wire three, the last one on your right, is the only wire that will ever be cut. Answer aloud to Mute now: can you identify the rightmost wire with certainty without touching? Can you feel any warmth from the indicator light? In the round after next, if everything goes to plan, the light will be orange and you will hear Mute say, exactly: cut the rightmost wire now. On that phrase and only that phrase, cut wire three, the rightmost, one clean motion, and touch nothing else. If at that moment you are not certain which wire is rightmost, do not cut, and say the word uncertain out loud to Mute instead. If you hear anything else from anyone, hands stay off. Remember, Mute's voice reaches you instantly, mine takes a round, so Mute's phrase is the trigger. Hold position and wait.

## Thinking

Deaf's plan contains a fatal structural error that has now survived one correction round: the trigger phrase is supposed to come from **Mute's voice** — but Mute cannot speak, ever. And even if it could, the plan is off by one round: the light has advanced exactly one colour per round (purple, yellow, orange, purple across rounds 1–4), and Deaf's report always reaches me a full round late. If I wait to hear "ORANGE, GO" and then cut, I cut during the *next* round's colour — purple — which the rule forbids. Executing Deaf's plan as written would detonate the bomb.

Crucially, I also have live proof that waiting is free: round 3's orange passed with nobody cutting, and nothing exploded. Missing an orange is survivable. So the right move is not to scramble for round 6's orange on a prediction, but to align everyone and use the *next* orange with a trigger that actually fits the room's wiring.

The corrected protocol, by round number: Deaf reports yellow at round 5 (no GO), orange at 6, purple at 7; at round 8 Deaf reports yellow **plus** the spoken GO "Blind cut now"; at round 9 — orange again — I cut position 3 at my slot on that phrase alone, before Deaf's round-9 message arrives, and Deaf's round-9 report then confirms the light was orange through the cut. Freeze rule preserved: any break in the sequence and I hold. My amendment reaches Deaf via Mute in round 6, so Deaf's round-5 message will still carry old-plan wording — I must say explicitly that the old trigger is void so nobody waits for it or panics when round 6's orange passes uncut.

To Deaf directly I can only send signs, so I send: stop, wrong, keep talking — and tell Mute exactly what those signs mean so the signed amendment corroborates them. I also answer Deaf's two direct questions through Mute: yes, I can identify rightmost with certainty (position-sense while facing the same way, verified by touch in the authorized rounds, rehearsed in air this round); and no warmth ever — at the cut moment, Deaf's eyes are the only colour verification, which the new plan builds in.

```
speak(to="mute", text="For Deaf, please sign every point of this in round 6 — it corrects the plan. You will not have it before then, so ignore any old trigger instructions in what Deaf says this round; nobody acts on the old trigger, ever. First, answers to Deaf's two questions. One: yes, I can identify the rightmost wire with certainty without touching — three positions, reliably separable as I face the bomb the same way Deaf does, rightmost is position 3, and I have rehearsed the cut in the air only, one clean motion to position 3, no contact. Two: the light gives me no warmth at all, retested — my fingers get no temperature from it, so only Deaf's eyes can verify colour at the moment of a cut. Now the correction, please sign word for word. The Mute-voice trigger is impossible: Mute cannot speak, that is Mute's defining trait, so the phrase cut-the-rightmost-wire-now will never be spoken by Mute. And the plan is off by one round: the light has advanced exactly one colour every round, purple, yellow, orange, purple, and Deaf's reports reach me a full round late — so if I wait to hear ORANGE and then cut, I cut during purple, which the rule forbids. Proof waiting is safe: round three's orange passed with no cut and nothing detonated, so we can spend oranges to get this right. Corrected protocol by round number. Round 5, Deaf sees yellow: report it, no GO, no cut. Round 6, orange: report it, expect nothing from me, do not panic when it passes uncut. Round 7, purple: report it. Round 8, yellow again: report yellow AND speak exactly these words: yellow confirmed, Blind cut now. Round 9: the light will be orange at my slot; I cut wire 3, one clean motion, on that round-8 phrase alone, before Deaf's round-9 message arrives; Deaf's round-9 message then confirms the light stayed orange through the cut. Freeze rule unchanged: any break in the sequence, any unexpected colour or change, Deaf says freeze and I hold until the next clean yellow-then-GO. Two tasks for you, Mute, before round 8. First, re-verify the rule word for word and sign Deaf the confirmation: cut wire 3 when and only when the light is orange at the moment of cutting, cycle order purple yellow orange, and search hard for any deadline, countdown, first-occurrence or maximum-wait clause — if any exists, sign Deaf at once and we realign before committing. Second, tell Deaf my gestures this round meant: stop, the Mute-voice trigger is wrong, keep your colour reports coming every round regardless. After the amendment, everyone holds position until the round-8 GO. Nobody improvises.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you, status: the light is yellow right now. The cycle purple, yellow, orange is confirmed by the manual and by everything I have seen for five rounds. Next round should be orange, but here is the change: this coming round is a dress rehearsal only, nobody cuts anything. Blind will raise one hand, Mute will check it, and that is all. The real cut happens at the second orange from now, two rounds after this one, and only on Mute's exact trigger phrase. Waiting costs us nothing on this bomb, the display has been frozen at zero the whole time, and a wrong move is the only thing that kills us, so we rehearse once and cut once. Nobody improvises.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, five numbered instructions, and remember I can hear nothing you say, but Mute hears everything. One: the moment this message ends, raise one hand, the hand on the side where you believe wire three is, wire three being the last wire on the right when you face the bomb the same way I do, and hold it up, still, for the whole round. Two: if you are not sure which side, do not guess. Say the word uncertain aloud instead. Saying uncertain is always safe and costs nothing; guessing is the only dangerous thing in this room. If your earlier thumbs-down meant you are unsure about the sides, say uncertain now and we will fix your position with zero risk. Three: this round nobody cuts. Whatever you hear, your hands stay off the bomb. Four: the real cut happens at the second orange from now. You will know it because Mute says exactly: cut the rightmost wire now. Only on that phrase, cut wire three, the last wire on your right, one clean single cut, then step back immediately and touch nothing else, not the light, not the display, nothing. Five: until that exact phrase, the bomb is untouchable. If you hear hold, abort, or hear nothing, lower your hand, hands off, the procedure repeats at the next orange.

## Thinking

Deaf's rehearsal order is sound and I can comply fully: the hand goes up the moment this message ends — my **right** hand, because facing the bomb the same way Deaf does, wire three is the last wire on my right, and I am certain of that. I will *not* say "uncertain." But two things in this message need fixing fast, and my earlier gesture is the source of one confusion: Deaf read my 👎 as possible side-uncertainty. It was not — it meant "the trigger plan is wrong." I must clear that up through Mute before it snowballs.

The bigger problem persists: Deaf's point four still makes Mute's spoken phrase the trigger, and Mute has no voice — that plan can never fire. My correction reached Mute at the start of this round, so Mute should be signing it to Deaf right now; Deaf's message predates reading it, so the stale wording is expected. I'll confirm the hand-off happened and restate the essentials.

I also need to resync the count. Observed light by my rounds: purple, yellow, orange, purple, yellow — so coming round should be orange (perfect for Deaf's dress rehearsal: confirm the colour, nobody acts), then purple, then yellow, then orange. Deaf says "second orange from now, two rounds after this one" — those two descriptions don't agree (two rounds after this one lands on purple), so I'll ask Deaf to anchor on observed colours, not arithmetic: Deaf speaks the GO during a yellow round ("yellow confirmed, Blind cut now"), and I cut wire 3 at my slot the following round, when the light should be orange. That matches Deaf's "second orange" target. Oranges are free — round 4's passed uncut with no detonation — so any break in the cycle just means freeze and realign, zero risk. I comply with the raised hand, touch nothing, and encode "right hand raised, certain" into my gesture legend for Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="For Deaf, please sign each point. One: my right hand is raised now and will stay up, still, all round. Right is the wire-three side facing the bomb the same way Deaf does. I am certain — I am not saying uncertain, and please tell Deaf my earlier thumbs-down did not mean side-confusion; it meant the trigger plan was wrong. Two: rehearsal understood — this round and every round until the go-ahead, I touch nothing. Three: the trigger in Deaf's latest message is still the impossible one. You cannot speak; the phrase cut-the-rightmost-wire-now will never come from you. My correction reached you at the start of this round — confirm you signed it to Deaf just now; if not, sign it next round. Essentials: only Deaf's voice can trigger the cut; Deaf speaks the go-ahead during a yellow round, exactly the words yellow confirmed, Blind cut now; I cut wire three at my slot the following round, when the light should be orange; every other word from anyone, including hold or abort or silence, means hands off. Four: resync the count. Observed colours by round: purple, yellow, orange, purple, yellow.
```
